% ── Shared helpers (available to all section files) ─────────
%  \speakerslide{Name}{Topics}
\newcommand{\speakerslide}[2]{%
  \begin{frame}{}
    \centering\vspace{0.5cm}
    \begin{beamercolorbox}[rounded=true,shadow=true,sep=8pt,
                           center,wd=0.80\linewidth]{block title}
      {\large\bfseries #1}
    \end{beamercolorbox}
    \vspace{0.4cm}
    \begin{beamercolorbox}[rounded=true,sep=6pt,
                           center,wd=0.80\linewidth]{block body}
      {\normalsize #2}
    \end{beamercolorbox}
  \end{frame}%
}

%  \slide{Frame Title}  — empty content placeholder
\newcommand{\slide}[1]{%
  \begin{frame}{#1}
    \vspace{0.6cm}
    \centering
    \textcolor{itiDark!35}{\itshape [ Fill in your content here ]}
  \end{frame}%
}

%  \screenshotslide{Frame Title}{relative/path/to/image}
%  ── Drop your screenshot file at the given path and compile.
%  ── Supported formats: .png  .jpg  .pdf
%  ── The image is scaled to fill 90 % of the frame width.
%  ── If the file is missing a labelled placeholder is shown instead.
% \safeimg{file}{width}{height}
%   Includes the image if the file exists; otherwise shows a placeholder box.
%   Uses a dedicated \newread register + bare \openin (no = or braces),
%   matching how LaTeX's own \IfFileExists works internally.
\makeatletter
\newread\@screenshotcheck
\newcommand{\safeimg}[3]{%
  \openin\@screenshotcheck #1 %
  \ifeof\@screenshotcheck
    \closein\@screenshotcheck
    \fbox{%
      \begin{minipage}[c][#3][c]{#2}%
        \centering
        {\small\itshape\color{itiDark} Screenshot not yet added}\\[6pt]
        {\ttfamily\tiny\color{itiDark} \detokenize{#1}}%
      \end{minipage}%
    }%
  \else
    \closein\@screenshotcheck
    \includegraphics[width=#2,height=#3,keepaspectratio]{#1}%
  \fi
}
\makeatother

\newcommand{\screenshotslide}[2]{%
  \begin{frame}{#1}
    \centering
    \safeimg{#2}{0.90\textwidth}{0.78\textheight}
  \end{frame}%
}

%  \screenshotpair{Frame Title}{Left caption}{Left image}{Right caption}{Right image}
%  ── Side-by-side screenshots (useful for before/after or two views)
\newcommand{\screenshotpair}[5]{%
  \begin{frame}{#1}
    \begin{columns}[c]
      \column{.48\textwidth}
        \centering
        {\footnotesize\bfseries #2}\\[4pt]
        \safeimg{#3}{\linewidth}{0.72\textheight}
      \column{.48\textwidth}
        \centering
        {\footnotesize\bfseries #4}\\[4pt]
        \safeimg{#5}{\linewidth}{0.72\textheight}
    \end{columns}
  \end{frame}%
}
